examples: That is an odd noise.
It was an odd hat.
The dog did something odd.

more.def: Strange or different from what is usual.
examples: It was odd to see snow in the spring.
The odd noise from the attic made us curious.
He had an odd way of walking, with a bounce.

easy.def: Not able to be shared into two equal groups.
examples: Three is an odd number.
Seven is odd.
One, three and five are odd numbers.

more.def: Describing a whole number that cannot be divided evenly by two, such as 1, 3 or 5.
examples: Seven is an odd number because it leaves one left over.
The odd numbers go 1, 3, 5, 7.
When you divide an odd number by two, you get a half left over.
It was an oddity.
The oddity was a square egg.
A strange oddity.
A purple tomato is an oddity.
The shop sold many oddities.
It was an oddity that the clock ran backward.

easy.def: The chance that something will happen.
examples: The odds of winning are small.
What are the odds?
The odds are good.

more.def: How likely it is that something will happen.
examples: The odds of winning the game are good.
The odds of rain are about one in two.
He beat the odds and won the race.

easy.def: A poem in praise of something.
examples: He wrote an ode to his dog.
The ode was long.
An ode to spring.

more.def: A poem that praises a person, place or thing.
examples: She wrote an ode to her dog.
The poet read an ode to the sea.
We wrote an ode to our school.
It was an odious task.
An odious smell.
The odious weed.
Cleaning the stinky drain was an odious task.
An odious smell filled the room.
The odious weed took over the garden.

easy.def: A smell, often a bad one.
examples: A strange odor filled the room.
The trash had a bad odor.
I noticed an odor.

more.def: A smell, especially one that is strong or unpleasant.
examples: A strong odor of fish filled the kitchen.
The gym bag had a bad odor after the game.
The soap left a pleasant odor in the air.
